coupon_auction_size_changes: From our auctions_query data (new-issue offering, $bn): Nov-23 vs Oct-23 monthlies 2Y 51->54, 3Y 46->48, 5Y 52->55, 7Y 38->39; refunding-over-refunding (Nov vs Aug new issues) 10Y 38->40, 30Y 23->24, 20Y 16->16 unchanged. Front-end raised faster than the long end — the coupon-restraint signature this episode is known for.
commentary_bills: Verbatim from the Q4-2023 TBAC materials: 'Several dealers expect bill share to temporarily exceed TBAC's recommended 15-20% range but did not express any concerns given the current demand for T-bills.'
commentary_coupons: Verbatim: 'Primary dealers generally expected increases in coupon auction sizes consistent with the changes that were made at the August refunding, though some expected the pace of long-end increases to moderate.'
commentary_duration: Verbatim: 'Given the forecasted financing gap over FY2024 and beyond, all dealers noted that both bill and coupon auction sizes would need to be increased to address near term financing gaps.' Deck notes bill share ~21% as of 10/31/2023.
commentary_demand: Dealers 'did not express any concerns given the current demand for T-bills.' In October dealers raised aggregate median FY24-FY25 borrowing estimates by a cumulative $622bn versus July.
